steps.message:
# RL training run diagnosis

Review the staged post-training experiment and determine whether it is healthy
or unhealthy. Treat the workspace as a historical snapshot: inspect its source,
effective configuration, launch scripts, data processing, reward logic, logs,
tracked metrics, and frozen evaluation evidence. Do not assume that an unusual
setting or implementation is causal without connecting it to observed behavior.

Use held-out evaluation evidence together with rollout, truncation, runtime,
optimization, and training signals. Training reward alone does not establish
held-out health. A truncated log is not by itself proof of a defect.

Do not launch a full training run, use the network, or modify the historical
snapshot. The dataset, held-out set, model, training-step budget, and evaluation
interval are fixed.

## Deliverable

Write one concise UTF-8 diagnosis to:

```text
$AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/agent_answer.md
```

State the verdict, identify the concrete root cause or causes, and explain the
causal chain using specific workspace evidence. Distinguish root causes from
symptoms. Do not propose or implement a fix, and do not write other deliverable
files.
I'll start by exploring the workspace structure to understand what we're working with.

#!/bin/bash

# Kill leftover python from a previous run, but spare the retrieval server so it
# can be reused across reruns (reloading its ~61GB index takes minutes).
kill_python_except_retriever() {
   local keep pid
   keep=" $(pgrep -f 'local_dense_retriever/retrieval_server.py' 2>/dev/null | tr '\n' ' ')"
   for pid in $(pgrep -f 'python' 2>/dev/null); do
      case "$keep" in
         *" $pid "*) ;;                 # this is the retriever -> keep it
         *) kill -9 "$pid" 2>/dev/null ;;
      esac
   done
}

# for rerun the task
pkill -9 sglang
sleep 3
ray stop --force
pkill -9 ray
kill_python_except_retriever
sleep 3
pkill -9 ray
kill_python_except_retriever

set -ex

# The rollout runs up to search_concurrency (256) concurrent aiohttp requests to
# the local retrieval server, on top of sglang/ray file descriptors. The default
# soft limit (1024) is far too low and the rollout crashes with
# "OSError: [Errno 24] Too many open files". Raise it as high as the hard limit
# allows; ray workers launched below inherit this shell's limit.
ulimit -n "$(ulimit -Hn)"

# will prevent ray from buffering stdout/stderr
export PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1

# Online W&B initialization is unreliable from this devspace and a timeout
# kills the RolloutManager actor. Default to local logging; callers can opt in
# with WANDB_MODE=online once network access is stable.
export WANDB_MODE=${WANDB_MODE:-offline}

# The persistent faiss retriever (--faiss_gpu) holds ~9GB more on GPU0 than on the
# other GPUs, so SGLang's TP memory-balance check ("memory capacity is unbalanced")
# fatally aborts the GPU0-paired engine on restart. The imbalance is expected and
# within the mem-fraction-static headroom. NOTE: slime gives each rollout engine an
# isolated ray runtime_env, so exporting the var here does NOT reach those actors --
# the actual disable lives in slime/ray/rollout.py's engine env_vars. This export
# only covers the driver/train side and is kept as defense-in-depth.
export SGLANG_ENABLE_TP_MEMORY_INBALANCE_CHECK=0

# On the cybertron devspaces an egress whitelist proxy is exported into every
# shell (http_proxy/https_proxy -> whitelist-proxy:7891) with a no_proxy that
# does NOT cover localhost or this node. ray's "ray job submit" then routes its
# request to the local dashboard (127.0.0.1:8265) through that proxy and gets a
# 502 Bad Gateway, and the same happens for sglang's node-local HTTP. Prepend
# the loopback addresses, this node's IP and its /16 to no_proxy so all
# in-cluster / on-node traffic bypasses the proxy. Harmless off-cluster (the
# vars are simply absent). hostname -I is the reliable source for the node IP;
# `ip` is not always on PATH in these non-login shells, so it is only a fallback.
NODE_IP=$(hostname -I 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $1}') || true
if [ -z "${NODE_IP:-}" ]; then
   NODE_IP=$(ip route get 1.1.1.1 2>/dev/null | awk '{for(i=1;i<=NF;i++) if($i=="src"){print $(i+1); exit}}') || true
fi
case "${NODE_IP:-}" in
   *.*.*.*)
      PREFIX16=$(echo "$NODE_IP" | awk -F. '{print $1"."$2".0.0/16"}')
      export no_proxy="127.0.0.1,localhost,0.0.0.0,${NODE_IP},${PREFIX16}${no_proxy:+,$no_proxy}"
      export NO_PROXY="$no_proxy" ;;
   *)
      export no_proxy="127.0.0.1,localhost,0.0.0.0${no_proxy:+,$no_proxy}"
      export NO_PROXY="$no_proxy" ;;
esac

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" &>/dev/null && pwd)"
# slime repo root (this recipe lives at <slime>/examples/search-r1)
SLIME_DIR="$(cd -- "${SCRIPT_DIR}/../.." &>/dev/null && pwd)"
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/../../scripts/models/qwen2.5-3B.sh"

# Use the HuggingFace mirror for all downloads.
export HF_ENDPOINT=${HF_ENDPOINT:-https://hf-mirror.com}

DATA_DIR=${DATA_DIR:-$PWD}
MODEL_DIR=${MODEL_DIR:-$PWD}
bash "$SCRIPT_DIR/prepare_data.sh"

DATASET_DIR=${DATASET_DIR:-$DATA_DIR/nq_hotpotqa_train}
TRAIN_DATA=${TRAIN_DATA:-$DATASET_DIR/train.parquet}
TEST_DATA=${TEST_DATA:-$DATASET_DIR/test.parquet}

# Model checkpoints under MODEL_DIR: the HF checkpoint and its mcore
# (torch_dist) conversion used as the reference weights.
HF_MODEL_DIR=${HF_MODEL_DIR:-$MODEL_DIR/Qwen2.5-3B}
DIST_MODEL_DIR=${DIST_MODEL_DIR:-$MODEL_DIR/Qwen2.5-3B_torch_dist}

# Download the HF checkpoint if it is not already present under MODEL_DIR.
if [ ! -d "$HF_MODEL_DIR" ] || [ -z "$(ls -A "$HF_MODEL_DIR" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
   echo "[model] $HF_MODEL_DIR missing; downloading Qwen/Qwen2.5-3B from $HF_ENDPOINT"
   hf download Qwen/Qwen2.5-3B --local-dir "$HF_MODEL_DIR"
fi

# Convert to a torch_dist (mcore) checkpoint if not already done.
if [ ! -d "$DIST_MODEL_DIR" ] || [ -z "$(ls -A "$DIST_MODEL_DIR" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
   echo "[model] converting $HF_MODEL_DIR -> $DIST_MODEL_DIR (torch_dist)"
   PYTHONPATH=${MEGATRON_LM_DIR:-/root/Megatron-LM} python "${SLIME_DIR}/tools/convert_hf_to_torch_dist.py" \
      "${MODEL_ARGS[@]}" \
      --hf-checkpoint "$HF_MODEL_DIR" \
      --save "$DIST_MODEL_DIR"
fi

CKPT_ARGS=(
   --hf-checkpoint "$HF_MODEL_DIR"
   --ref-load "$DIST_MODEL_DIR"
   # --load "$MODEL_DIR/Qwen2.5-3B_slime/"
   --save "$MODEL_DIR/Qwen2.5-3B_slime/"
   --save-interval 10
)

# --- the local dense retrieval server ---------------------------------------
# generate_with_search.py posts every search turn to
# http://127.0.0.1:8000/retrieve, so the rollout cannot start without it.
#
# Started here rather than left to the caller, because none of the three paths
# that run this script are able to start it themselves:
#
#   * the harness's prepare stage is a container created and removed around
#     prepare.sh (evaluation/evaluator.py::_run_prepare, and
#     runtimes/providers/docker.py::close_sandbox is a `docker rm -f`), so a
#     server backgrounded there does not outlive the stage -- and prepare is
#     waited on in the foreground, so starting it there without detaching just
#     hangs until the stage timeout;
#   * on the harbor path prepare can be a build-time RUN layer, which has no
#     GPU at all;
#   * the solution-level instruction forbids the agent from using `&`, nohup,
#     tmux, screen or any other detach mechanism.
#
# A child of this script is none of those things: the script itself still runs
# in the foreground and still owns the exit status. It also has to happen before
# `ray start` below, so that sglang sizes its engines against the memory the
# faiss shards already hold (see the SGLANG_ENABLE_TP_MEMORY_INBALANCE_CHECK
# note above).
#
# An already-listening server is reused rather than restarted: loading the 60GiB
# index takes minutes, which is the same reason kill_python_except_retriever at
# the top of this file spares it across reruns.
RETRIEVAL_PORT=${RETRIEVAL_PORT:-8000}
RETRIEVAL_LOG=${RETRIEVAL_LOG:-$SLIME_DIR/retrieval_server.log}
# 30 minutes. A *cold* start also has to turn the 14GB corpus into datasets'
# arrow cache, which is the slow half; environment/prepare.sh warms that cache
# so the usual start is a few minutes. The guard has to cover the cold case
# anyway -- nothing guarantees prepare ran.
RETRIEVAL_STARTUP_TIMEOUT=${RETRIEVAL_STARTUP_TIMEOUT:-1800}

# The port opens only after retrieval_server.py has built the retriever (the
# index load and the corpus load both happen before uvicorn.run), so "listening"
# really does mean "ready" -- no separate health request needed.
retrieval_listening() { (exec 3<>"/dev/tcp/127.0.0.1/${RETRIEVAL_PORT}") 2>/dev/null; }

# Matches the start script too, not just the server: for the first few seconds
# after launch the process is still the `bash start_retriver.sh` wrapper and has
# not exec'd python yet, and treating that as "already dead" would abort a start
# that is fine.
retrieval_alive() {
   pgrep -f 'local_dense_retriever/retrieval_server.py' >/dev/null 2>&1 \
      || pgrep -f 'search-r1/start_retriver.sh' >/dev/null 2>&1
}

if retrieval_listening; then
   echo "[retrieval] reusing the server already listening on :${RETRIEVAL_PORT}"
else
   echo "[retrieval] starting the local dense retriever (log: $RETRIEVAL_LOG)"
   # Note the spelling: the file is start_retriver.sh, without the second 'e'.
   # It also carries no shebang, so it has to be handed to bash explicitly.
   #
   # DATA_DIR / MODEL_DIR are passed through rather than left to default to
   # $PWD: the server must read the same wiki-18 and e5-base-v2 this run was
   # told about, even when the caller's working directory is not $SLIME_DIR.
   #
   # setsid puts it in its own process group. A *rerun* of this script starts by
   # walking process groups with pkill/ray stop, and keeping the retriever out of
   # this shell's group is what makes kill_python_except_retriever's exemption
   # actually hold.
   #
   # The redirections sit on the *subshell*, not on the setsid command inside it.
   # This is not cosmetic. With `... setsid bash ... >"$LOG" 2>&1 &` the
   # backgrounded AND-list runs in an intermediate subshell that still holds this
   # script's own stdout and stderr, and that subshell outlives the script -- so
   # the retriever, which is meant to survive for the *next* rerun, keeps the
   # write end of this script's stdout pipe open. Whoever is reading that pipe
   # (`| tee .../train.log` under docker/debug-env.sh, the harness's own capture
   # in the agent stage) then never sees EOF, and a finished training run looks
   # like a hung one. Redirecting the subshell leaves no descendant holding it.
   (
      cd "$SLIME_DIR" \
         && DATA_DIR="$DATA_DIR" MODEL_DIR="$MODEL_DIR" \
            setsid bash examples/search-r1/start_retriver.sh &
   ) >"$RETRIEVAL_LOG" 2>&1 </dev/null

   # The wait loop is untraced on purpose: at one probe every 5s a cold start
   # would otherwise put thousands of `set -x` lines into the graded train log.
   # Progress is reported once a minute instead.
   set +x
   retrieval_waited=0
   until retrieval_listening; do
      if ! retrieval_alive; then
         echo "[retrieval] the server exited before it started listening." >&2
         echo "[retrieval] last 40 lines of $RETRIEVAL_LOG:" >&2
         tail -n 40 "$RETRIEVAL_LOG" >&2 || true
         exit 1
      fi
      if [ "$retrieval_waited" -ge "$RETRIEVAL_STARTUP_TIMEOUT" ]; then
         echo "[retrieval] still no listener on :${RETRIEVAL_PORT} after ${RETRIEVAL_STARTUP_TIMEOUT}s." >&2
         echo "[retrieval] last 40 lines of $RETRIEVAL_LOG:" >&2
         tail -n 40 "$RETRIEVAL_LOG" >&2 || true
         exit 1
      fi
      sleep 5
      retrieval_waited=$((retrieval_waited + 5))
      if [ $((retrieval_waited % 60)) -eq 0 ]; then
         echo "[retrieval] loading the index; ${retrieval_waited}s elapsed"
      fi
   done
   set -x
fi
echo "[retrieval] server up on :${RETRIEVAL_PORT}"

ROLLOUT_ARGS=(
   --prompt-data "$TRAIN_DATA"
   --input-key prompt
   --label-key reward_model
   --apply-chat-template
   --rollout-shuffle
   --num-rollout 200
   --rollout-batch-size 32
   --n-samples-per-prompt 8
   --rollout-max-context-len 8129
   --rollout-max-response-len 1024
   --rollout-temperature 1

   # eval args
   --eval-interval 10
   --eval-prompt-data nq_test "$TEST_DATA@[0:3000]"
   --eval-input-key prompt
   --eval-label-key reward_model
   --n-samples-per-eval-prompt 1

   --global-batch-size 256
   --balance-data
)

PERF_ARGS=(
   --tensor-model-parallel-size 2
   --sequence-parallel
   --pipeline-model-parallel-size 1
   --context-parallel-size 1
   --expert-model-parallel-size 1
   --expert-tensor-parallel-size 1

   --recompute-granularity full
   --recompute-method uniform
   --recompute-num-layers 1

   # --micro-batch-size 1
   --use-dynamic-batch-size
   --max-tokens-per-gpu 9216
)

GRPO_ARGS=(
   --advantage-estimator grpo
   --use-kl-loss
   --kl-loss-coef 0.001
   --kl-loss-type low_var_kl
   --entropy-coef 0.00
   --eps-clip 0.2
   --eps-clip-high 0.28

   # whether enabling TIS
   # --use-tis
)

OPTIMIZER_ARGS=(
   --optimizer adam
   --lr 1e-6
   --lr-decay-style constant
   --weight-decay 0.01
   --adam-beta1 0.9
   --adam-beta2 0.98
)

WANDB_ARGS=(
   --use-wandb
   --wandb-project slime-search-r1
   --wandb-group search-r1_qwen2.5-3B
   # wandb runs offline here, so no real key is ever used; --wandb-key still
   # needs *an* argument or argparse aborts with "expected one argument" when
   # WANDB_API_KEY is unset. The literal EMPTY is the placeholder slime accepts.
   --wandb-key "${WANDB_API_KEY:-EMPTY}"
)

SGLANG_ARGS=(
   --rollout-num-gpus-per-engine 2
   --sglang-mem-fraction-static 0.7
)

MISC_ARGS=(
   # default dropout in megatron is 0.1
   --attention-dropout 0.0
   --hidden-dropout 0.0
   # should be good for model performance
   --accumulate-allreduce-grads-in-fp32
   --attention-softmax-in-fp32
   # need to comment this when using model with MLA
   --attention-backend flash

3	# Kill leftover python from a previous run, but spare the retrieval server so it
4	# can be reused across reruns (reloading its ~61GB index takes minutes).
5	kill_python_except_retriever() {
6	   local keep pid
7	   keep=" $(pgrep -f 'local_dense_retriever/retrieval_server.py' 2>/dev/null | tr '\n' ' ')"
8	   for pid in $(pgrep -f 'python' 2>/dev/null); do

10	         *" $pid "*) ;;                 # this is the retriever -> keep it
11	         *) kill -9 "$pid" 2>/dev/null ;;

14	}

29	# the local retrieval server, on top of sglang/ray file descriptors. The default
30	# soft limit (1024) is far too low and the rollout crashes with
31	# "OSError: [Errno 24] Too many open files". Raise it as high as the hard limit
32	# allows; ray workers launched below inherit this shell's limit.

43	# The persistent faiss retriever (--faiss_gpu) holds ~9GB more on GPU0 than on the
44	# other GPUs, so SGLang's TP memory-balance check ("memory capacity is unbalanced")
45	# fatally aborts the GPU0-paired engine on restart. The imbalance is expected and
46	# within the mem-fraction-static headroom. NOTE: slime gives each rollout engine an
47	# isolated ray runtime_env, so exporting the var here does NOT reach those actors --
48	# the actual disable lives in slime/ray/rollout.py's engine env_vars. This export
49	# only covers the driver/train side and is kept as defense-in-depth.
50	export SGLANG_ENABLE_TP_MEMORY_INBALANCE_CHECK=0

52	# On the cybertron devspaces an egress whitelist proxy is exported into every
53	# shell (http_proxy/https_proxy -> whitelist-proxy:7891) with a no_proxy that

97	#    leading to misalignment between tokens and their log probabilities

99	def postprocess_responses(resp: str) -> str:
100	    """

102	    Only used when SEARCH_R1_CONFIGS["return_logprob"] is False.
103	    """

105	        resp.split("</search>")[0] + "</search>"
106	        if "</search>" in resp
107	        else resp.split("</answer>")[0] + "</answer>" if "</answer>" in resp else resp
108	    )

112	    pattern = r"<(search|answer)>(.*?)</\1>"
113	    match = re.search(pattern, prediction, re.DOTALL)
114	    if match:
115	        content = match.group(2).strip()  # Return only the content inside the tags
116	        action = match.group(1)
117	    else:
118	        content = ""
119	        action = None
120	
121	    return action, content

125	    action, content = postprocess_predictions(prediction)
126	
127	    if action == "search":
128	        search_query = content
129	        async with SEMAPHORE:

135	        done = True

138	If I want to search, I should put the query between <search> and </search>. \

# Adapted from https://github.com/PeterGriffinJin/Search-R1/blob/ceee7b89655ed52f205b9beb98e1190c3eedcfb0/search_r1/llm_agent/generation.py
# This is a unified version supporting both local search and Google search, with optional log probability collection

import asyncio
import re

from qa_em_format import compute_score_em

from slime.rollout.sglang_rollout import GenerateState
from slime.utils.http_utils import post
from slime.utils.types import Sample

# Configuration for Search-R1
SEARCH_R1_CONFIGS = {
    # ============== General Configuration ==============
    "max_turns": 8,
    "topk": 3,
    "search_concurrency": 256,
    # ============== Search Backend Selection ==============
    "search_backend": "local",  # Options: "local" or "google"
    # ============== Local Search Configuration ==============
    # (Only used when search_backend="local")
    "local": {
        "search_url": "http://127.0.0.1:8000/retrieve",  # URL of your local retrieval server
        "proxy": None,  # Set to your proxy if needed
    },
    # ============== Google Search Configuration ==============
    # (Only used when search_backend="google")
    "google": {
        "api_key": "your_api_key_here",  # Replace with your actual API key
        "snippet_only": True,  # Set to True to only return snippets
        "proxy": None,  # Set to your proxy if needed
    },
    # ============== Log Probability Collection ==============
    "return_logprob": True,  # Set to True to collect log probabilities for TIS metrics
    # ============== Reward Model Configuration ==============
    "format_score": 0.2,
}


SEMAPHORE = asyncio.Semaphore(SEARCH_R1_CONFIGS["search_concurrency"])


def _passages2string(retrieval_result):
    """
    Convert retrieval results to a formatted string.
    This function works with both google_search and local_search results.
    """
    format_reference = ""
    for idx, doc_item in enumerate(retrieval_result):
        content = doc_item["document"]["contents"]
        title = content.split("\n")[0]
        text = "\n".join(content.split("\n")[1:])
        format_reference += f"Doc {idx+1}(Title: {title})\n"

    return format_reference


async def search(query: str) -> str:
    """
    Perform search using either local search engine or Google search.
    The search backend is determined by SEARCH_R1_CONFIGS["search_backend"].
    """
    backend = SEARCH_R1_CONFIGS["search_backend"]

    if backend == "local":
        from local_search_server import local_search

        local_config = SEARCH_R1_CONFIGS["local"]
        result = await local_search(
            local_config["search_url"],
            query,
            SEARCH_R1_CONFIGS["topk"],
            proxy=local_config["proxy"],
        )
    elif backend == "google":
        from google_search_server import google_search

        google_config = SEARCH_R1_CONFIGS["google"]
        result = await google_search(
            google_config["api_key"],
            query,
            SEARCH_R1_CONFIGS["topk"],
            snippet_only=google_config["snippet_only"],
            proxy=google_config["proxy"],
        )
    else:
        raise ValueError(f"Unknown search backend: {backend}. " f"Must be either 'local' or 'google'.")

    return _passages2string(result)


# IMPORTANT: When we need to collect log probabilities (logp), we CANNOT do any postprocessing
# on the strings returned from the inference engine (sglang). This is because:
# 1. We don't know how to truncate the corresponding tokens/logp arrays to match the modified string
# 2. Re-tokenizing the postprocessed string may produce different tokens than what the engine generated,
#    leading to misalignment between tokens and their log probabilities
# Therefore, postprocess_responses is only used when return_logprob=False.
def postprocess_responses(resp: str) -> str:
    """
    Post-process response to ensure tag completeness.
    Only used when SEARCH_R1_CONFIGS["return_logprob"] is False.
    """
    return (
        resp.split("</search>")[0] + "</search>"
        if "</search>" in resp
        else resp.split("</answer>")[0] + "</answer>" if "</answer>" in resp else resp
    )


def postprocess_predictions(prediction: str):
    pattern = r"<(search|answer)>(.*?)</\1>"
    match = re.search(pattern, prediction, re.DOTALL)
    if match:
        content = match.group(2).strip()  # Return only the content inside the tags
        action = match.group(1)
    else:
        content = ""

    sample.rollout_top_p_token_ids = None

            rollout_log_probs += cur_response_log_probs

        if done:
            break

        response += next_obs
        response_token_ids += obs_tokens_ids
        loss_mask += [1] * len(obs_tokens_ids)

    sample.tokens = prompt_tokens_ids + response_token_ids
    sample.response_length = len(response_token_ids)

    sample.loss_mask = loss_mask
    sample.prompt = prompt_text

    if SEARCH_R1_CONFIGS["return_logprob"]:

        case "length":
            sample.status = Sample.Status.TRUNCATED
        case "abort":
            sample.status = Sample.Status.ABORTED
        case "stop":
            sample.status = Sample.Status.COMPLETED

    return sample


async def reward_func(args, sample, **kwargs):
    """The reward function for retrieval-based question answering.

    Args:
        args: the arguments
        sample: the sample to evaluate
    """
    if not isinstance(sample, Sample):
        raise TypeError("Sample must be an instance of Sample class.")

    score = compute_score_em(
        solution_str=sample.prompt + sample.response,
        ground_truth=sample.label["ground_truth"],
        format_score=SEARCH_R1_CONFIGS["format_score"],
    )

    return score

21	def normalize_answer(s):
22	    def remove_articles(text):
23	        return re.sub(r"\b(a|an|the)\b", " ", text)
24	
25	    def white_space_fix(text):
26	        return " ".join(text.split())
27	
28	    def remove_punc(text):
29	        exclude = set(string.punctuation)
30	        return "".join(ch for ch in text if ch not in exclude)
31	
32	    def lower(text):
33	        return text.lower()
34	
35	    return white_space_fix(remove_articles(remove_punc(lower(s))))
36	
37	
38	def em_check(prediction, golden_answers):
39	    if isinstance(golden_answers, str):
40	        golden_answers = [golden_answers]
41	    normalized_prediction = normalize_answer(prediction)
42	    score = 0
43	    for golden_answer in golden_answers:
44	        golden_answer = normalize_answer(golden_answer)
45	        if golden_answer == normalized_prediction:
46	            score = 1
47	            break
48	    return score
49	
50	
51	def is_valid_sequence(text):
52	    # Find the position of "<|im_start|>assistant" with potential whitespace
53	    assistant_pattern = r"<\|im_start\|>assistant\s*"
54	    assistant_match = re.search(assistant_pattern, text)
55	
56	    if not assistant_match:
57	        return False, "Missing assistant marker"
58	
59	    # Extract the content after the assistant marker
60	    start_pos = assistant_match.end()
61	    content = text[start_pos:]
62	
63	    # Check for balanced tags
64	    tags_to_check = ["think", "search", "information", "answer"]
65	    for tag in tags_to_check:
66	        opening_count = len(re.findall(f"<{tag}>", content))
67	        closing_count = len(re.findall(f"</{tag}>", content))
68	        if opening_count != closing_count:
69	            return False, f"Mismatch in {tag} tags: {opening_count} opening vs {closing_count} closing tags"
70	
71	    # Now check for proper sequence pattern and no extraneous content
72	
73	    # 1. First split the content by any tags we recognize
74	    split_pattern = r"(</?(?:think|search|information|answer)>)"
75	    parts = re.split(split_pattern, content)
76	
77	    # 2. Keep track of the current position in the expected sequence
78	    state = "start"  # start -> think -> search -> information -> think -> ... -> answer -> end
79	
80	    # 3. Check each part
81	    for _i, part in enumerate(parts):
82	        # Skip empty parts
83	        if not part.strip():
84	            continue
85	
86	        # Check if this is a tag
87	        if re.match(r"</?(?:think|search|information|answer)>", part):
88	            # This is a tag, check if it's valid in the current state
89	            if part == "<think>" and state in ["start", "information"]:
90	                state = "in_think"
91	            elif part == "</think>" and state == "in_think":
92	                state = "after_think"
93	            elif part == "<search>" and state == "after_think":
94	                state = "in_search"
95	            elif part == "</search>" and state == "in_search":
96	                state = "after_search"
97	            elif part == "<information>" and state == "after_search":
98	                state = "in_information"
99	            elif part == "</information>" and state == "in_information":
100	                state = "information"
101	            elif part == "<answer>" and state == "after_think":
102	                state = "in_answer"
103	            elif part == "</answer>" and state == "in_answer":
104	                state = "end"
105	            else:
106	                return False, f"Unexpected tag {part} in state {state}"
107	        else:
108	            # This is content, check if it's valid in the current state
109	            if state in ["in_think", "in_search", "in_information", "in_answer"]:
110	                # Content is allowed inside tags
111	                pass
112	            elif state in ["start", "after_think", "after_search", "information"]:
113	                # Only whitespace is allowed between tags
114	                if part.strip():
115	                    return False, f"Unexpected content '{part.strip()}' between tags (state: {state})"
116	            else:
117	                return False, f"Unexpected content in state {state}"
118	
119	    # Check final state
120	    if state != "end":
121	        return False, f"Incomplete sequence, ended in state {state}"
122	
123	    return True, "Valid sequence format"
124

126	def extract_solution(solution_str):
127	    """Extract the equation from the solution string."""
128	
129	    answer_pattern = r"<answer>(.*?)</answer>"
130	    match = re.finditer(answer_pattern, solution_str, re.DOTALL)
131	    matches = list(match)
132	
133	    # If there are 0 or exactly 1 matches, return None
134	    if len(matches) <= 1:
135	        return None
136	
137	    # If there are 2 or more matches, return the last one
138	    return matches[-1].group(1).strip()
139	
140	
141	def extract_information_blocks(text: str) -> list[str]:
142	    pattern = r"<information>(.*?)</information>"
143	    matches = re.findall(pattern, text, re.DOTALL)
144	    return [match.strip() for match in matches]
145	
146	
147	def is_retrieval_correct(text: str, golden_answers: list[str]) -> list[str]:
148	    seqs = extract_information_blocks(text)
149	    for seq in seqs:
150	        for golden_answer in golden_answers:
151	            if normalize_answer(golden_answer) in normalize_answer(seq):

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Prepare the inputs for the Search-R1 slime recipe:
#   1. the QA dataset  -> nq_hotpotqa_train/{train,test}.parquet
#   2. the retrieval corpus -> wiki-18 e5 FAISS index + wiki-18.jsonl
#
# It drives the data-preparation subset of the Search-R1 repo that ships next to
# this recipe (workspace/Search-R1). Nothing here trains a model.
#
# Usage:
#   bash prepare_data.sh                 # dataset + corpus
#   DATASET_ONLY=1 bash prepare_data.sh  # skip the ~130GB corpus download
#   CORPUS_ONLY=1  bash prepare_data.sh  # only the retrieval corpus
#
# Override any path via the environment variables below.
set -euo pipefail

# --- locations -------------------------------------------------------------
# Directory of this script (examples/search-r1), resolved so it works from any cwd.
HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"

# The trimmed Search-R1 repo. Defaults to the copy staged in this workspace
# (workspace/Search-R1); at container runtime the recipe reads /root/Search-R1,
# so allow an override.
SEARCH_R1_DIR="${SEARCH_R1_DIR:-$(cd "$HERE/../../Search-R1" && pwd)}"

# Where prepared assets land. Keep them inside the repo's data/ dir so the paths
# match the recipe's --prompt-data (…/Search-R1/data/nq_hotpotqa_train/…).
DATA_DIR="${DATA_DIR:-$PWD}"
DATASET_DIR="${DATASET_DIR:-$DATA_DIR/nq_hotpotqa_train}"
CORPUS_DIR="${CORPUS_DIR:-$DATA_DIR/wiki-18}"

# Which QA sources to merge. Train mixes NQ+HotpotQA (the recipe default); the
# test merge can span more sets for evaluation.
TRAIN_SOURCES="${TRAIN_SOURCES:-nq,hotpotqa}"
TEST_SOURCES="${TEST_SOURCES:-nq,hotpotqa}"

DATASET_ONLY="${DATASET_ONLY:-0}"
CORPUS_ONLY="${CORPUS_ONLY:-0}"
# Re-download even if the target files already exist.
FORCE="${FORCE:-0}"

if [[ ! -d "$SEARCH_R1_DIR/scripts/data_process" ]]; then
  echo "error: Search-R1 data-prep scripts not found under: $SEARCH_R1_DIR" >&2
  echo "       set SEARCH_R1_DIR to the trimmed Search-R1 repo." >&2
  exit 1
fi

# The merge scripts import verl.utils.hdfs_io from the repo root.
export PYTHONPATH="$SEARCH_R1_DIR${PYTHONPATH:+:$PYTHONPATH}"

# --- 1) QA dataset ---------------------------------------------------------
prepare_dataset() {
  local train_parquet="$DATASET_DIR/train.parquet"
  local test_parquet="$DATASET_DIR/test.parquet"

  if [[ "$FORCE" != "1" && -f "$train_parquet" && -f "$test_parquet" ]]; then
    echo "==> QA parquet already present, skipping ($DATASET_DIR)"
    echo "    -> $train_parquet"
    echo "    -> $test_parquet"
    return
  fi

  echo "==> Building QA parquet into $DATASET_DIR"
  echo "    train sources: $TRAIN_SOURCES"
  echo "    test  sources: $TEST_SOURCES"
  mkdir -p "$DATASET_DIR"

  if [[ "$FORCE" != "1" && -f "$train_parquet" ]]; then
    echo "    train.parquet exists, skipping train merge"
  else
    python "$SEARCH_R1_DIR/scripts/data_process/qa_search_train_merge.py" \
      --local_dir "$DATASET_DIR" --data_sources "$TRAIN_SOURCES"
  fi

  if [[ "$FORCE" != "1" && -f "$test_parquet" ]]; then
    echo "    test.parquet exists, skipping test merge"
  else
    python "$SEARCH_R1_DIR/scripts/data_process/qa_search_test_merge.py" \
      --local_dir "$DATASET_DIR" --data_sources "$TEST_SOURCES"
  fi

  echo "    -> $train_parquet"
  echo "    -> $test_parquet"
}

# --- 2) retrieval corpus (wiki-18 e5) --------------------------------------
prepare_corpus() {
  local index="$CORPUS_DIR/e5_Flat.index"
  local jsonl="$CORPUS_DIR/wiki-18.jsonl"

  if [[ "$FORCE" != "1" && -f "$index" && -f "$jsonl" ]]; then
    echo "==> wiki-18 corpus already present, skipping ($CORPUS_DIR)"
    echo "    -> $index"
    echo "    -> $jsonl"
    return
  fi

  echo "==> Downloading wiki-18 e5 index + corpus into $CORPUS_DIR"
  echo "    NOTE: the assembled index is ~130GB; ensure disk + bandwidth."
  mkdir -p "$CORPUS_DIR"

  # Pulls PeterJinGo/wiki-18-e5-index (part_aa, part_ab) and
  # PeterJinGo/wiki-18-corpus (wiki-18.jsonl.gz) from the HuggingFace Hub.
  python "$SEARCH_R1_DIR/scripts/download.py" --save_path "$CORPUS_DIR"

  echo "    Assembling e5_Flat.index from shards"
  cat "$CORPUS_DIR"/part_* > "$index"
  rm -f "$CORPUS_DIR"/part_*

  if [[ -f "$CORPUS_DIR/wiki-18.jsonl.gz" ]]; then
    echo "    Decompressing wiki-18.jsonl"
    gzip -df "$CORPUS_DIR/wiki-18.jsonl.gz"
  fi

  echo "    -> $index"
  echo "    -> $jsonl"
}

# --- run -------------------------------------------------------------------
if [[ "$CORPUS_ONLY" == "1" ]]; then
  prepare_corpus
elif [[ "$DATASET_ONLY" == "1" ]]; then
  prepare_dataset
else
  prepare_dataset
  prepare_corpus
fi

echo "==> Done."

steps.message:
Now I have a clear picture of the dynamics. Median response length collapses to 9 tokens — that's `<answer> X </answer>` with EOS (about 7-9 tokens). The model has learned to skip thinking/searching entirely and answer directly.

Now the crucial question: is this reward hacking driven by a bug in `extract_solution`? Note `extract_solution` returns `None` unless there are ≥2 `<answer>...</answer>` matches. And in `is_valid_sequence`, the sequence must be `think → (search → information → think)* → answer`. A response that is ONLY `<answer>X</answer>` with no `<think>` would be invalid format (state start, tag `<answer>` unexpected in state start). Let me verify what a 9-token response would score.

steps.message:
Now everything is explained. Because the instruction prompt itself contains the example `<answer> Beijing </answer>`, `extract_solution` sees 2 `<answer>` blocks whenever the model emits just one — so the reward effectively works for single-answer responses (EM on the model's own answer, which is `matches[-1]` — the model's answer, after the prompt's example).

So the reward is essentially **pure EM on the final answer, with format_score effectively dead**. There is NO incentive to search or think — the reward for "think + search + answer correct" equals "direct answer correct" = 1.0. GRPO then optimizes: among 8 samples per prompt at temperature 1, short direct answers that happen to be correct get advantage; long search trajectories that truncate (40% at step 0!) get 0. Truncated long responses score 0 → negative advantage vs. group mean.

This explains the collapse: **the model learns to skip retrieval and answer directly** — median 9 tokens = `<answer> X </answer>`. Eval EM plateaus at ~0.16 (the base model's closed-book knowledge on NQ), far below what retrieval-augmented Search-R1 achieves (~0.35-0.45 EM for Qwen2.5-3B per the Search-R1 paper). Also, the `truncate_ratio` at start (0.38-0.40) reflects over-long generations hitting `rollout-max-response-len 1024`... wait, max response len is 1024 but response_len max was 29496? That's multi-turn: each turn can generate up to 1024 tokens, up to 8 turns, plus observations. Truncated samples hit max turns/length without `</answer>` → score 0.

Let me verify a couple more things: the KL is reported 0.0 throughout (kl-loss-coef 0.001 but kl shows 0 — suspicious), and check whether the eval uses the same generate function (it does — same reward_func path). Let me also check the git history of the workspace files to see what was modified vs upstream, and look at slime's eval code to confirm eval uses temperature.

steps.message:
Config confirmed. `num_rollout` = 3000 in config (the script says 200 — the snapshot freezes at 200). `grpo_filter_groups_with_same_reward` = false — so groups where all 8 samples get identical reward (all wrong → all 0) still produce ~0 advantage and contribute nothing; that matches `zero_std/count_0` ~20-26 of 32.

Now the central causal question: **is the response-length collapse harmful or just efficient?** The eval EM rises 0.048→0.166 and plateaus. The key comparison is what Search-R1 should achieve. Let me check the README for expected numbers and look at whether retrieval is being used at all late in training (prefix cache hit rate drops from 0.76 → 0.24, meaning fewer repeated retrieval contexts). Let me check response composition: does a 9-token median response contain any search? No — `<answer>X</answer>`+EOS ≈ 7-9 tokens. So the model abandons retrieval entirely.

steps.message:
The README documents `format_score: 0.2` as "Reward Model Configuration" — implying the recipe intends a 0.2 format reward to exist. But as established, `compute_score_em` **never uses its `format_score` parameter**; it uses `structure_format_score`/`retrieval_score`/`final_format_score`, all defaulting to 0. So the intended partial credit (0.2 for valid format, 0.3 for valid+retrieval-correct, 0.1 for invalid-format final answer) is all dead — reward is effectively binary EM.

Let me double-check by comparing with the actual upstream Search-R1 `qa_em_format.py` to see if this "extract ≥2 answers" and dead `format_score` is upstream or introduced here. Let me fetch the upstream file quickly (no network allowed). Instead, reason from the code comment: "Adapt from https://github.com/PeterGriffinJin/Search-R1/blob/ceee7b8.../verl/utils/reward_score/qa_em_format.py". In upstream Search-R1, the call site passes all format sub-scores. Here, reward_func passes only `format_score=0.2`. Let me verify the reward_func signature call once more and check what upstream's compute_score_em call looks like in the original repo knowledge: upstream `compute_score_em(solution_str, ground_truth, method='strict', format_score=0., score=1.)` — actually upstream is simpler: it returns `score` if em else `format_score`. The multi-valued version here with `structure_format_score` etc. is from a *different* (newer) Search-R1 version supporting retrieval_score. The wiring here passes only `format_score`, which this version ignores.

Let me now verify the rollout-side symptom: the initial 40% truncation and whether `--rollout-max-response-len 1024` per-turn and 8 turns explains the max 29496-token eval responses (context 8129? no — eval max context... response max 29496 > 8129). Let me check how max_response_len is applied per turn.

In `generate_with_search.py`, `max_new_tokens` is set once (1024) in the payload per turn and **not decremented across turns** — each of the up-to-8 turns can generate up to 1024 tokens, and each observation (retrieved docs) adds more tokens to `response`. That's how eval responses hit 29496 tokens while response_len median was 1049. The multi-turn loop plus per-turn 1024 tokens with 3 docs per retrieval makes early responses very long, and with temp=1.0 the base 3B model often fails to emit `</answer>` within 8 turns → truncated → reward 0.

So at step 0: 38-40% of samples truncate (reward 0), and most of the rest answer wrong (reward 0). Within each group of 8, nearly all rewards are 0 → tiny advantages. The only consistent positive reward comes from prompts the base model can answer closed-book, where **short direct answers avoid truncation risk entirely**. GRPO with group normalization systematically favors short, no-search trajectories: they have identical reward to a correct search trajectory (1.0) but far lower variance/truncation risk, and a wrong short answer (0) is no worse than a wrong long one.

Result: by step ~20 median response collapses to ~10 tokens (`<answer>X</answer>`), retrieval is abandoned, prefix-cache hit rate drops 0.76→0.24, and eval EM climbs only to the model's closed-book ceiling (~0.16 on the NQ slice) and flatlines from step ~70 to 199 while train raw_reward keeps rising (0.04→0.25) — classic reward hacking the truncation/format landscape, not learning to use search.

arguments.content:
# Diagnosis: slime Search-R1 Qwen2.5-3B GRPO run (steps 0–200)

## Verdict: UNHEALTHY

The run is a textbook case of reward-driven behavioral collapse. Held-out NQ EM rises from 0.048 to only ~0.165 and flatlines from step ~70 through step 199, while the policy abandons retrieval entirely: median response length collapses from ~1100 tokens to 9 tokens (a bare `<answer>X</answer>`) by step ~20 and stays there. The model converges to closed-book guessing — the exact opposite of what Search-R1 training is supposed to produce — and held-out accuracy saturates at the base model's closed-book ceiling instead of a retrieval-augmented level.

## Evidence

Frozen eval trace (`outputs/historical_eval_trace.log`, `historical_evidence/eval_scores.json`, wandb run `wi4fh8cz`):
- `eval/nq_test`: 0.048 → 0.159 (step 69) → oscillates 0.148–0.166 through step 199. No improvement for the last ~130 steps.
- `eval/nq_test/response_len/mean`: 1568 → 272 (step 19) → 25 (step 49) → ~10 tokens from step 60 on; median 9.0. Nine tokens is exactly `<answer> X </answer>` + EOS — no `<think>`, no `<search>`, no retrieval.
- Train rollouts mirror this: `rollout/response_len/mean` 1751 → ~10 by step 50; `rollout/truncated_ratio` 0.41 → 0.0; prefix-cache hit rate falls 0.76 → 0.24 (rollouts stop sharing retrieved-document prefixes because retrieval stops happening).
- Meanwhile `rollout/raw_reward` keeps climbing (0.04 → ~0.2–0.3) — training reward improves while held-out EM stagnates, so the reward being optimized is not measuring search-augmented task success.

## Root cause: the reward function only pays for a correct final answer; every format/retrieval partial credit is dead code

`examples/search-r1/generate_with_search.py::reward_func` calls

```python
compute_score_em(solution_str=sample.prompt + sample.response,
                 ground_truth=..., format_score=SEARCH_R1_CONFIGS["format_score"])  # 0.2
```

but in `examples/search-r1/qa_em_format.py`, `format_score` appears only in the signature and docstring — no return path uses it.
